messages:
customer-jdoe: Hey team — noticed a big surge in token usage tied to a streaming session. Safari user sees partial EventSource output (a couple events) then the stream stalls and the client reconnects repeatedly. Net effect: lots of short streams, partial outputs, and a billing spike. Repro steps below.

jess: Sorry for the trouble — can you paste the client request + the response headers you see at the edge? Also which CDN/cloud front door are you using?

customer-jdoe: Client: `new EventSource('/api/v1/stream?session=abc', { withCredentials: true })` on Safari 16.3. Server demo headers (from origin):
```
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: public, max-age=120
ETag: "abc123"
Vary: Accept-Encoding
```
Edge logs show some 304 responses for the same URL then 200 chunked responses. We also see a couple 401s mid-stream when our auth token rotated.

mike: Two likely problems combined: (1) CDN returning cached/304 responses for an SSE endpoint — Safari is known to buffer or stall EventSource when it receives certain caching/304 behaviors; (2) token rotation causing mid-stream 401 which triggers client reconnect. Together that explains reconnect loop + billing.

alice: Quick repro to validate: run a tiny origin that streams events every 2s with the headers you posted; put Cloudflare/fastly in front configured to cache based on ETag; open in Safari and in Chrome. Chrome usually keeps emitting; Safari will often hold and then reconnect. Also try with an EventSource polyfill (eg `event-source-polyfill`) — polyfills can change reconnect timing and make the billing hit worse.

customer-jdoe: We confirmed: Chrome smooth, Safari stalls. With the polyfill, reconnects are ~1.5s and we burned tokens.

jess: For immediate mitigation: 1) disable CDN caching on the streaming path (turn off ETag/If-Modified-Since handling for `/api/v1/stream`), 2) ensure the stream response has explicit no-cache headers, 3) avoid rotating the token while a stream is active (rotate proactively).

mike: Server-side recommended headers for SSE:
```
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate
Pragma: no-cache
Connection: keep-alive
Vary: Authorization
```
Also avoid setting ETag/Last-Modified on streaming endpoints. If you must put a front door, configure the edge to treat `/stream` as non-cacheable and pass Authorization through.

alice: For auth token churn: best practice is to renew tokens and then start a new stream, or use short-lived stream-specific tokens that remain valid for stream lifetime. If the control plane issues a 401 midstream, do not rely on client to retry immediately — have backoff and jitter configured.

jess: Support action: paused billing escalation and opened an internal P0. Assigning to eng-runtime + eng-infra for CDN rules. @mike @alice please coordinate.

mike: Creating a small fix: ensure our proxy strip ETag and set `Cache-Control: private, max-age=0` for `/v1/stream` and add `Vary: Authorization`. Will push to staging in ~4h, prod in ~24h after smoke tests. Also adding an entry to docs about SSE and edge caching.

support-bot: Incident SR-2026-0457 created and linked to this thread.

customer-jdoe: Thanks — this is P0 for a paying customer, please ping me when staging is up.

mike: Will post the staging link and a quick smoke script. Example curl to test (use `-N` to disable buffering):
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://staging.redwood.ai/api/v1/stream?session=test
```
Run in Safari after updating CDN rule to confirm no 304s/ETag and that events stream continuously.

jess: Noted. I'll keep the customer updated. If you need immediate workaround, tell the customer to disable the polyfill on Safari or use the mobile/web app that uses the native WebSocket alternative.

customer-jdoe: Understood — disabling polyfill reduced reconnect frequency. Appreciate the quick triage.

mike: Will follow up with deploy notes and the doc PR.
